raw: CHAPTER XIII. The Fellow of No Delicacy
en: [Chapter 13] The Fellow of No Delicacy

raw: If Sydney Carton ever shone anywhere, he certainly never shone in the house of Doctor Manette.
en: If Sydney Carton ever showed any spark of his former self, he certainly never did so at the home of Doctor Manette.
ko: 만약 시드니 카턴이 과거의 자신의 모습을 조금이라도 보여준 적이 있다면, 적어도 마네트 박사의 집에서는 결코 그런 적이 없었다.

raw: He had been there often, during a whole year, and had always been the same moody and morose lounger there.
en: He had visited frequently over the past year, but had always been the same gloomy and depressed lounger.
ko: 그는 지난 한 해 동안 자주 방문했지만, 언제나 똑같이 우울하고 의기소침한 게으름뱅이의 모습이었다.

raw: When he cared to talk, he talked well; but, the cloud of caring for nothing, which overshadowed him with such a fatal darkness, was very rarely pierced by the light within him.
en: When he chose to talk, he spoke well; but his habit of caring about nothing, which cast a dark shadow over him, was rarely broken by his inner intelligence.
ko: 그가 대화를 하기로 마음먹었을 때 그는 말을 잘했지만; 그에게 짙은 그림자를 드리운 아무것도 신경 쓰지 않는 습관은 내면의 지성에 의해 깨지는 일이 거의 없었다.

raw: And yet he did care something for the streets that environed that house, and for the senseless stones that made their pavements.
en: Yet he did care for the streets around that house, and for the very stones of the pavement.
ko: 하지만 그는 그 집 주변의 거리와 심지어 포장도로의 돌멩이들에게까지 마음을 썼다.

raw: Many a night he vaguely and unhappily wandered there, when wine had brought no transitory gladness to him; many a dreary daybreak revealed his solitary figure lingering there, and still lingering there when the first beams of the sun brought into strong relief, removed beauties of architecture in spires of churches and lofty buildings, as perhaps the quiet time brought some sense of better things, else forgotten and unattainable, into his mind.
en: Many a night he wandered there unhappily, when wine failed to bring even temporary cheer. Many a gloomy dawn found his solitary figure lingering there, even when the first rays of the sun lit up the church spires and tall buildings. Perhaps these quiet hours brought back memories of better things, now forgotten and out of reach.
ko: 술이 일시적인 기쁨조차 가져다주지 못할 때, 그는 수많은 밤을 그곳에서 불행하게 헤매었다. 우울한 수많은 새벽은 태양의 첫 광선이 교회 첨탑과 높은 건물들을 비출 때조차도 그곳을 서성이는 그의 고독한 모습을 발견했다. 아마도 이 조용한 시간들은 지금은 잊혀지고 닿을 수 없는 더 나은 것들에 대한 기억을 다시 불러일으켰을지도 모른다.

raw: Of late, the neglected bed in the Temple Court had known him more scantily than ever; and often when he had thrown himself upon it no longer than a few minutes, he had got up again, and haunted that neighbourhood.
en: Lately, he rarely slept in his bed in the Temple, often getting up after only a few minutes to wander around Soho.
ko: 최근에 그는 템플의 침대에서 잠을 자는 일이 거의 없었고, 단 몇 분 만에 일어나 소호 주변을 헤매곤 했다.

raw: On a day in August, when Mr.
en: On a day in August, after Mr.
ko: 팔월의 어느 날, 미스터

raw: Stryver (after notifying to his jackal that “he had thought better of that marrying matter”) had carried his delicacy into Devonshire, and when the sight and scent of flowers in the City streets had some waifs of goodness in them for the worst, of health for the sickliest, and of youth for the oldest, Sydney’s feet still trod those stones.
en: Stryver had informed his assistant that "he had changed his mind about marrying," taking his blunt manners to Devonshire, Sydney's feet still walked those streets. The sight and smell of flowers in the city streets brought a touch of joy to the poorest, health to the sick, and a feeling of youth to the old.
ko: 스트라이버가 그의 조수에게 "결혼에 대한 마음을 바꿨다"고 알리고 퉁명스러운 태도를 데번셔로 가져간 후에도, 시드니의 발걸음은 여전히 그 거리를 걷고 있었다. 도시 거리의 꽃들의 모습과 향기는 가장 가난한 사람들에게는 약간의 기쁨을, 병자들에게는 건강을, 노인들에게는 젊음의 느낌을 가져다주었다.

raw: From being irresolute and purposeless, his feet became animated by an intention, and, in the working out of that intention, they took him to the Doctor’s door.
en: Instead of being unsure and having no purpose, his steps suddenly gained a clear goal, and following that goal, they led him straight to the Doctor's door.
ko: 확신이 없고 목적이 없는 대신, 그의 발걸음은 갑자기 명확한 목표를 얻었고, 그 목표를 따라 그를 박사의 문 앞까지 곧장 이끌었다.

raw: He was shown up-stairs, and found Lucie at her work, alone.
en: He was shown upstairs and found Lucie working alone.
ko: 그는 위층으로 안내되었고 루시가 혼자 일하고 있는 것을 보았다.

raw: She had never been quite at her ease with him, and received him with some little embarrassment as he seated himself near her table.
en: She had never felt quite comfortable around him, and received him with some embarrassment as he sat near her table.
ko: 그녀는 결코 그를 꽤 편안하게 느낀 적이 없었고, 그가 그녀의 테이블 근처에 앉았을 때 약간의 당혹감을 느끼며 그를 맞이했다.

raw: But, looking up at his face in the interchange of the first few common-places, she observed a change in it.
en: But looking at his face as they exchanged greetings, she noticed a change in him.
ko: 하지만 그들이 인사를 나눌 때 그의 얼굴을 바라보면서, 그녀는 그에게서 변화를 알아차렸다.

raw: “I fear you are not well, Mr.
en: "I fear you are not well, Mr.
ko: "당신의 건강이 좋지 않은 것 같아 걱정이에요, 미스터

raw: Carton!”
en: Carton!"
ko: 카턴!"

raw: “No.
en: "No.
ko: "아닙니다.

raw: But the life I lead, Miss Manette, is not conducive to health.
en: But the life I lead, Miss Manette, is not healthy.
ko: 하지만 제가 영위하는 삶은 건강하지 않습니다, 마네트 양.

raw: What is to be expected of, or by, such profligates?”
en: What else can be expected of a man like me?"
ko: 저 같은 남자에게 그 외에 무엇을 기대할 수 있겠습니까?"

raw: “Is it not--forgive me; I have begun the question on my lips--a pity to live no better life?”
en: "Is it not, forgive me for asking, a pity to live such a life?"
ko: "이런 질문을 드려 죄송하지만, 그런 삶을 사는 것이 안타깝지 않으신가요?"

raw: “God knows it is a shame!”
en: "God knows it is a shame!"
ko: "신은 그것이 부끄러운 일임을 아십니다!"

raw: “Then why not change it?”
en: "Then why not change it?"
ko: "그렇다면 왜 그것을 바꾸지 않으시나요?"

raw: Looking gently at him again, she was surprised and saddened to see that there were tears in his eyes.
en: Looking at him gently, she was surprised and saddened to see tears in his eyes.
ko: 부드럽게 그를 바라보며, 그녀는 그의 눈에 고인 눈물을 보고 놀랐고 슬퍼했다.

raw: There were tears in his voice too, as he answered:
en: His voice trembled as he answered:
ko: 대답할 때 그의 목소리가 떨렸다:

raw: “It is too late for that.
en: "It is too late for that.
ko: "그러기에는 너무 늦었습니다.

raw: I shall never be better than I am.
en: I will never be better than I am.
ko: 저는 결코 지금보다 나아지지 않을 것입니다.

raw: I shall sink lower, and be worse.”
en: I will only sink lower and get worse."
ko: 저는 오직 더 깊이 가라앉고 더 나빠질 뿐입니다."

raw: He leaned an elbow on her table, and covered his eyes with his hand.
en: He rested his elbow on the table and covered his eyes with his hand.
ko: 그는 팔꿈치를 테이블에 기대고 손으로 자신의 눈을 가렸다.

raw: The table trembled in the silence that followed.
en: The table shook in the silence that followed.
ko: 이어지는 침묵 속에서 테이블이 흔들렸다.

raw: She had never seen him softened, and was much distressed.
en: She had never seen him show such feeling and was deeply distressed.
ko: 그녀는 그가 그런 감정을 보이는 것을 결코 본 적이 없었고 깊이 괴로워했다.

raw: He knew her to be so, without looking at her, and said:
en: Sensing her concern without looking up, he said:
ko: 고개를 들지 않은 채 그녀의 염려를 감지하며, 그가 말했다:

raw: “Pray forgive me, Miss Manette.
en: "Please forgive me, Miss Manette.
ko: "저를 용서하십시오, 마네트 양.

raw: I break down before the knowledge of what I want to say to you.
en: I break down when I try to say what I want to tell you.
ko: 당신에게 드리고 싶은 말씀을 하려고 할 때마다 저는 무너져 내립니다.

raw: Will you hear me?”
en: Will you listen to me?"
ko: 제 말씀을 들어주시겠습니까?"

raw: “If it will do you any good, Mr.
en: "If it will help you, Mr.
ko: "만약 그것이 당신에게 도움이 된다면, 미스터

raw: Carton, if it would make you happier, it would make me very glad!”
en: Carton, or make you happier, I would gladly listen!"
ko: 카턴, 혹은 당신을 더 행복하게 해준다면, 기꺼이 듣겠어요!"

raw: “God bless you for your sweet compassion!”
en: "God bless you for your sweet compassion!"
ko: "당신의 다정한 연민에 신의 축복이 있기를 바랍니다!"

raw: He unshaded his face after a little while, and spoke steadily.
en: He uncovered his face after a moment and spoke steadily.
ko: 잠시 후 그는 얼굴을 드러내고 흔들림 없이 말했다.

raw: “Don’t be afraid to hear me.
en: "Don't be afraid to listen.
ko: "듣는 것을 두려워하지 마십시오.

raw: Don’t shrink from anything I say.
en: Don't shrink from what I say.
ko: 제가 드리는 말씀에서 위축되지 마십시오.

raw: I am like one who died young.
en: I am like a man who died young.
ko: 저는 젊은 나이에 죽은 사람과 같습니다.

raw: All my life might have been.”
en: My life might have been so much more."
ko: 제 삶은 훨씬 더 의미 있었을지도 모릅니다."

raw: “No, Mr.
en: "No, Mr.
ko: "아니에요, 미스터

raw: Carton.
en: Carton.
ko: 카턴.

raw: I am sure that the best part of it might still be; I am sure that you might be much, much worthier of yourself.”
en: I am sure the best part of your life is still ahead of you. You could be much more worthy of yourself."
ko: 당신 삶의 가장 좋은 부분은 여전히 당신 앞에 있다고 확신해요. 당신은 당신 자신에게 훨씬 더 가치 있는 사람이 될 수 있어요."

raw: “Say of you, Miss Manette, and although I know better--although in the mystery of my own wretched heart I know better--I shall never forget it!”
en: "You mean worthy of you, Miss Manette. Although I know that is impossible, I will never forget that you said so!"
ko: "당신에게 가치 있는 사람이 될 수 있다는 뜻이군요, 마네트 양. 비록 그것이 불가능하다는 것을 알지만, 당신이 그렇게 말씀하셨다는 것을 저는 결코 잊지 않을 것입니다!"

raw: She was pale and trembling.
en: She was pale and trembling.
ko: 그녀는 창백해진 채 떨고 있었다.

raw: He came to her relief with a fixed despair of himself which made the interview unlike any other that could have been holden.
en: He spoke with a quiet despair that made the conversation unlike any other.
ko: 그는 그 대화를 다른 어떤 것과도 다르게 만드는 조용한 절망과 함께 말했다.

raw: “If it had been possible, Miss Manette, that you could have returned the love of the man you see before yourself--flung away, wasted, drunken, poor creature of misuse as you know him to be--he would have been conscious this day and hour, in spite of his happiness, that he would bring you to misery, bring you to sorrow and repentance, blight you, disgrace you, pull you down with him.
en: "If it had been possible, Miss Manette, for you to return the love of the man before you, wasted, drunk, and ruined as you know him to be, he would have known, even in his happiness, that he would bring you only misery, sorrow, and disgrace. I know you cannot love me.
ko: "만약 당신 앞에 있는 남자, 당신이 알고 있듯이 허비되고 취했으며 파멸한 이 남자의 사랑에 당신이 보답하는 것이 가능했더라면, 마네트 양, 그는 행복 속에서도 자신이 당신에게 비참함과 슬픔, 그리고 수치심만을 가져올 것임을 알았을 것입니다. 당신이 저를 사랑할 수 없다는 것을 저는 압니다.

raw: I know very well that you can have no tenderness for me; I ask for none; I am even thankful that it cannot be.”
en: I ask for no love, and I am even glad that it is impossible."
ko: 저는 어떠한 사랑도 요구하지 않으며, 심지어 그것이 불가능하다는 사실에 기쁩니다."

raw: “Without it, can I not save you, Mr.
en: "Without love, can I not help you, Mr.
ko: "사랑이 없다면, 제가 당신을 도울 수 없을까요, 미스터

raw: Carton?
en: Carton?
ko: 카턴?

raw: Can I not recall you--forgive me again!--to a better course?
en: Can I not guide you to a better path?
ko: 제가 당신을 더 나은 길로 인도할 수는 없을까요?

raw: Can I in no way repay your confidence?
en: Can I repay your trust in no way?
ko: 제가 당신의 신뢰에 보답할 방법이 전혀 없나요?

raw: I know this is a confidence,” she modestly said, after a little hesitation, and in earnest tears, “I know you would say this to no one else.
en: "I know you're trusting me with a secret," she said modestly, after hesitating a bit and shedding genuine tears. "I know you wouldn't say this to anyone else."
ko: "당신이 저를 믿고 비밀을 털어놓고 계신다는 걸 알아요." 약간 망설이며 진심 어린 눈물을 흘린 후, 그녀가 겸손하게 말했다. "다른 누구에게도 이런 말씀을 하지 않으시리라는 걸 알아요."

raw: Can I turn it to no good account for yourself, Mr. Carton?”
en: "Can I do nothing for you?"
ko: "제가 당신을 위해 아무것도 할 수 없나요?"

raw: He shook his head.
en: He shook his head.
ko: 그는 고개를 저었다.

raw: “To none.
en: "Nothing.
ko: "아무것도 없습니다.

raw: No, Miss Manette, to none.
en: No, Miss Manette, nothing.
ko: 아닙니다, 마네트 양, 아무것도 없습니다.

raw: If you will hear me through a very little more, all you can ever do for me is done.
en: If you will listen to me for just a moment more, you will have done all you can do.
ko: 만약 당신이 제게 조금만 더 귀를 기울여 주신다면, 당신이 할 수 있는 모든 것을 하신 것입니다.

raw: I wish you to know that you have been the last dream of my soul.
en: I want you to know that you have been the last dream of my soul.
ko: 당신이 제 영혼의 마지막 꿈이었다는 것을 당신이 알아주시기를 바랍니다.

raw: In my degradation I have not been so degraded but that the sight of you with your father, and of this home made such a home by you, has stirred old shadows that I thought had died out of me.
en: In my ruined life, the sight of you with your father in this beautiful home has stirred old hopes I thought were dead.
ko: 제 파멸한 삶 속에서, 이 아름다운 집에서 아버지와 함께 있는 당신의 모습은 죽었다고 생각했던 오랜 희망들을 불러일으켰습니다.

raw: Since I knew you, I have been troubled by a remorse that I thought would never reproach me again, and have heard whispers from old voices impelling me upward, that I thought were silent for ever.
en: Since I met you, I have felt a remorse I thought I would never feel again, and have heard old voices telling me to improve.
ko: 당신을 만난 이후로, 저는 다시는 느끼지 못할 줄 알았던 회한을 느꼈고, 제게 더 나아지라고 말하는 오래된 목소리들을 들었습니다.

raw: I have had unformed ideas of striving afresh, beginning anew, shaking off sloth and sensuality, and fighting out the abandoned fight.
en: I have had ideas of trying again, shaking off my laziness, and fighting the battle I had given up.
ko: 저는 나태함을 떨쳐내고 제가 포기했던 전투를 싸우며 다시 시도해보려는 생각들을 가졌습니다.

raw: A dream, all a dream, that ends in nothing, and leaves the sleeper where he lay down, but I wish you to know that you inspired it.”
en: It was a dream that ends in nothing, leaving me where I fell, but I want you to know that you inspired it."
ko: 그것은 제가 쓰러진 곳에 저를 남겨둔 채 아무것도 아닌 것으로 끝나는 꿈이었지만, 저는 당신이 그 꿈에 영감을 주었다는 것을 알아주시길 바랍니다."

raw: “Will nothing of it remain?
en: "Will nothing of it remain?
ko: "그중 아무것도 남지 않게 될까요?

raw: O Mr.
en: Oh, Mr.
ko: 오, 미스터

raw: Carton, think again!
en: Carton, think again!
ko: 카턴, 다시 생각해 보세요!

raw: Try again!”
en: Try again!"
ko: 다시 시도해 보세요!"

raw: “No, Miss Manette; all through it, I have known myself to be quite undeserving.
en: "No, Miss Manette. I have always known I am unworthy.
ko: "아닙니다, 마네트 양. 저는 제가 가치 없는 사람이라는 것을 항상 알고 있었습니다.

raw: And yet I have had the weakness, and have still the weakness, to wish you to know with what a sudden mastery you kindled me, heap of ashes that I am, into fire--a fire, however, inseparable in its nature from myself, quickening nothing, lighting nothing, doing no service, idly burning away.”
en: Yet I was weak enough to want you to know that you turned this heap of ashes into a fire, a fire that does no good and simply burns itself out."
ko: 그러나 저는 당신이 이 잿더미를 불로, 아무런 쓸모도 없이 단지 스스로 타버릴 뿐인 불로 바꾸었다는 것을 당신이 알아주기를 바랄 만큼 충분히 나약했습니다."

raw: “Since it is my misfortune, Mr.
en: "Since it is my misfortune, Mr.
ko: "그것이 저의 불행이므로, 미스터

raw: Carton, to have made you more unhappy than you were before you knew me--”
en: Carton, to have made you more unhappy than before, "
ko: 카턴, 당신을 이전보다 더 불행하게 만든 것이 말이에요, "

raw: “Don’t say that, Miss Manette, for you would have reclaimed me, if anything could.
en: "Don't say that, Miss Manette. You would have saved me if anything could.
ko: "그런 말씀은 하지 마십시오, 마네트 양. 무언가 저를 구원할 수 있었다면 당신이 저를 구원하셨을 것입니다.

raw: You will not be the cause of my becoming worse.”
en: You will not make me worse."
ko: 당신은 저를 더 나쁘게 만들지 않을 것입니다."

raw: “Since the state of your mind that you describe, is, at all events, attributable to some influence of mine--this is what I mean, if I can make it plain--can I use no influence to serve you?
en: "Since the state of mind you just described is, no matter what, caused by some influence of mine—this is what I'm trying to explain, if I can make it clear—can I use any of my influence to help you?"
ko: "어찌 되었든 당신이 방금 묘사하신 마음 상태가 저의 어떤 영향으로 인해 야기된 것이기 때문에—제가 분명히 말씀드릴 수 있다면, 이것이 제가 설명하려고 하는 것입니다—당신을 돕기 위해 제가 저의 어떠한 영향력이라도 사용할 수 있을까요?"

raw: Have I no power for good, with you, at all?”
en: Do I have no power for good with you at all?"
ko: 저에게는 당신과 관련하여 선을 행할 힘이 전혀 없는 건가요?"

raw: “The utmost good that I am capable of now, Miss Manette, I have come here to realise.
en: "The only good I am capable of now, Miss Manette, I have come to do today.
ko: "제가 지금 할 수 있는 유일한 선행을, 마네트 양, 저는 오늘 하러 왔습니다.

raw: Let me carry through the rest of my misdirected life, the remembrance that I opened my heart to you, last of all the world; and that there was something left in me at this time which you could deplore and pity.”
en: Let me carry through the rest of my life the memory of opening my heart to you, and knowing there was something in me you could pity."
ko: 당신에게 제 마음을 열었고, 제 안에 당신이 연민을 느낄 수 있는 무언가가 있었다는 것을 아는 그 기억을 제 남은 평생 동안 간직하게 해주십시오."

raw: “Which I entreated you to believe, again and again, most fervently, with all my heart, was capable of better things, Mr.
en: "Which I begged you to believe was capable of better things, Mr.
ko: "그리고 저는 그것이 더 나은 일들을 할 수 있다고 당신이 믿어주시기를 간청했어요, 미스터

raw: Carton!”
en: Carton!"
ko: 카턴!"

raw: “Entreat me to believe it no more, Miss Manette.
en: "Do not ask me to believe that, Miss Manette.
ko: "제게 그것을 믿으라고 요구하지 마십시오, 마네트 양.

raw: I have proved myself, and I know better.
en: I know myself too well.
ko: 저는 제 자신을 너무나도 잘 압니다.

raw: I distress you; I draw fast to an end.
en: I am upsetting you, and I must finish.
ko: 제가 당신을 속상하게 하고 있으니, 저는 끝마쳐야 합니다.

raw: Will you let me believe, when I recall this day, that the last confidence of my life was reposed in your pure and innocent breast, and that it lies there alone, and will be shared by no one?”
en: Will you allow me to believe, when I remember this day, that the last confidence of my life was placed in your pure keeping, and will be shared with no one else?"
ko: 제가 이 날을 기억할 때, 제 인생의 마지막 비밀이 당신의 순수한 보호 아래 맡겨졌으며 다른 누구와도 공유되지 않을 것이라고 믿도록 허락해 주시겠습니까?"

raw: “If that will be a consolation to you, yes.”
en: "If that brings you comfort, yes."
ko: "그것이 당신에게 위안을 가져다준다면, 네."

raw: “Not even by the dearest one ever to be known to you?”
en: "Not even by the person you will one day love most?"
ko: "당신이 언젠가 가장 사랑하게 될 사람에게조차도 말입니까?"

raw: “Mr.
en: She answered after a pause, "Mr.
ko: 그녀는 잠시 멈춘 후 대답했다, "미스터

raw: Carton,” she answered, after an agitated pause, “the secret is yours, not mine; and I promise to respect it.”
en: Carton, the secret is yours, not mine, and I promise to keep it."
ko: 카턴, 그 비밀은 제 것이 아니라 당신의 것이며, 저는 그것을 지키겠다고 약속합니다."

raw: “Thank you.
en: "Thank you.
ko: "감사합니다.

raw: And again, God bless you.”
en: And again, God bless you."
ko: 그리고 다시 한번, 신의 축복이 당신에게 있기를 바랍니다."

raw: He put her hand to his lips, and moved towards the door.
en: He kissed her hand and moved toward the door.
ko: 그는 그녀의 손에 입을 맞추고 문을 향해 이동했다.

raw: “Be under no apprehension, Miss Manette, of my ever resuming this conversation by so much as a passing word.
en: "Do not worry, Miss Manette, that I will ever bring this up again.
ko: "제가 이 이야기를 다시 꺼낼까 봐 걱정하지 마십시오, 마네트 양.

raw: I will never refer to it again.
en: I will never refer to it.
ko: 저는 그것을 결코 다시 언급하지 않을 것입니다.

raw: If I were dead, that could not be surer than it is henceforth.
en: It is as secure as if I were dead.
ko: 그것은 마치 제가 죽은 것처럼 안전합니다.

raw: In the hour of my death, I shall hold sacred the one good remembrance--and shall thank and bless you for it--that my last avowal of myself was made to you, and that my name, and faults, and miseries were gently carried in your heart.
en: In my last hour, I will cherish the memory that my last honest confession was made to you, and that my name and faults were carried gently in your heart.
ko: 제 생의 마지막 순간에, 저는 제 마지막 정직한 고백이 당신에게 이루어졌으며 제 이름과 허물들이 당신의 마음속에 부드럽게 간직되었다는 그 기억을 소중히 여길 것입니다.

raw: May it otherwise be light and happy!”
en: I hope your life is bright and happy!"
ko: 당신의 삶이 밝고 행복하기를 바랍니다!"

raw: He was so unlike what he had ever shown himself to be, and it was so sad to think how much he had thrown away, and how much he every day kept down and perverted, that Lucie Manette wept mournfully for him as he stood looking back at her.
en: He was so different from his usual self, and it was so sad to think of his wasted talents, that Lucie wept for him as he looked back.
ko: 그는 평소의 자신과 너무나 달랐고, 그의 허비된 재능을 생각하니 너무나 슬퍼서, 루시는 그가 뒤돌아볼 때 그를 위해 눈물을 흘렸다.

raw: “Be comforted!” he said, “I am not worth such feeling, Miss Manette.
en: "Be comforted!" he said. "I am not worth your tears, Miss Manette.
ko: "마음을 추스르십시오!" 그가 말했다. "저는 당신의 눈물을 받을 가치가 없습니다, 마네트 양.

raw: An hour or two hence, and the low companions and low habits that I scorn but yield to, will render me less worth such tears as those, than any wretch who creeps along the streets.
en: In an hour, the low companions and bad habits I hate but yield to will make me less worthy of your tears than any beggar on the street.
ko: 한 시간 안에, 제가 증오하지만 굴복하고 마는 저열한 동료들과 나쁜 습관들이 길거리의 어떤 거지보다도 저를 당신의 눈물에 더 가치 없는 사람으로 만들 것입니다.

raw: Be comforted!
en: Be comforted!
ko: 마음을 추스르십시오!

raw: But, within myself, I shall always be, towards you, what I am now, though outwardly I shall be what you have heretofore seen me.
en: But in my heart, I will always be toward you what I am now.
ko: 하지만 제 마음속에서, 저는 항상 지금의 모습으로 당신을 대할 것입니다.

raw: The last supplication but one I make to you, is, that you will believe this of me.”
en: My last request but one is that you believe this."
ko: 저의 마지막에서 두 번째 부탁은 당신이 이것을 믿어주시는 것입니다."

raw: “I will, Mr.
en: "I will, Mr.
ko: "그러겠어요, 미스터

raw: Carton.”
en: Carton."
ko: 카턴."

raw: “My last supplication of all, is this; and with it, I will relieve you of a visitor with whom I well know you have nothing in unison, and between whom and you there is an impassable space.
en: "My last request of all is this: I will now leave you, a visitor with whom you have nothing in common.
ko: "저의 가장 마지막 부탁은 이것입니다: 저는 이제 당신과 아무런 공통점도 없는 방문객으로서 당신을 떠날 것입니다.

raw: It is useless to say it, I know, but it rises out of my soul. For you, and for any dear to you, I would do anything.
en: It is useless to say, but it comes from my soul: for you, and for anyone dear to you, I would do anything.
ko: 말해봤자 소용없는 일이지만, 그것은 제 영혼에서 우러나온 것입니다: 당신을 위해서, 그리고 당신이 소중히 여기는 그 누구를 위해서라도, 저는 어떤 일이든 할 것입니다.

raw: If my career were of that better kind that there was any opportunity or capacity of sacrifice in it, I would embrace any sacrifice for you and for those dear to you.
en: If my life had any value or opportunity for sacrifice, I would gladly sacrifice it for you and those you love.
ko: 만약 제 삶에 어떤 가치나 희생의 기회가 있다면, 저는 당신과 당신이 사랑하는 사람들을 위해 기꺼이 그것을 희생할 것입니다.

raw: Try to hold me in your mind, at some quiet times, as ardent and sincere in this one thing.
en: Try to keep me in your thoughts during your quiet moments, and remember that I am passionate and sincere about this one thing.
ko: 당신의 조용한 시간 동안에 저를 기억해 주시기를, 그리고 이 한 가지에 대해서만큼은 제가 열정적이고 진심이라는 것을 기억해 주시기를 바랍니다.

raw: The time will come, the time will not be long in coming, when new ties will be formed about you--ties that will bind you yet more tenderly and strongly to the home you so adorn--the dearest ties that will ever grace and gladden you.
en: The time will come, and it won't be long, when new bonds will form around you—bonds that will connect you even more tenderly and strongly to the home you make so beautiful—the most precious bonds that will ever bless and bring you joy.
ko: 머지않아 당신 주변에 새로운 유대 관계가 형성될 때가 올 것입니다—당신이 그토록 아름답게 만드는 가정에 당신을 훨씬 더 다정하고 강하게 연결해 줄 유대 관계, 당신을 축복하고 기쁨을 가져다줄 가장 소중한 유대 관계가 말입니다.

raw: O Miss Manette, when the little picture of a happy father’s face looks up in yours, when you see your own bright beauty springing up anew at your feet, think now and then that there is a man who would give his life, to keep a life you love beside you!”
en: Oh, Miss Manette, when you look at a happy child's face, or see your own beauty reflected in your children, remember that there is a man who would gladly give his life to keep the life you love beside you!"
ko: 오, 마네트 양, 당신이 행복한 아이의 얼굴을 보거나 당신의 아이들에게 비친 당신 자신의 아름다움을 볼 때, 당신이 사랑하는 생명을 당신 곁에 지키기 위해 기꺼이 자신의 목숨을 바칠 한 남자가 있다는 것을 기억해 주십시오!"

raw: He said, “Farewell!” said a last “God bless you!” and left her.
en: He said, "Farewell!" and left her.
ko: 그는 "안녕히 계십시오!"라고 말하고 그녀를 떠났다.
